_about: Question bank for calls and interviews with an employer. Seeds the questions_to_employer field in analysis_report.py. Each entry is a pattern, not a script: the generator must tie it to a specific line in the job ad. Sources: Improve Business Academy, Effective Job Creation Strategies, slide 'What to say when you call (or write)?' (course); the owner's own examples (owner, 2026-10-01); the Hamamatsu and Veo call prep (derived).

stages.pre_application_call: Short call or email before applying. Goal: one fact the ad does not say, a contact name, a good first impression. Three questions, five minutes.
stages.interview: Questions at the end of an interview. Goal: judge fit and show how you think.

patterns.first_month: What to focus on in the first month
patterns.success: What success looks like at 6-12 months
patterns.task_detail: A task named in the ad, in more detail
patterns.challenges: Current challenges the role should address
patterns.collaborators: Who you work with, cross-department work
patterns.what_to_highlight: What to highlight in the application
patterns.onboarding: How new people are trained and onboarded
patterns.requirement_weight: How strict a stated requirement is

questions.text: What are the most important tasks I should focus on during the first month?
What does success in this role look like in the first 6-12 months?
Could you describe {task from the ad} in a bit more detail?
questions.use_when: The ad names a task in one vague line.

questions.text: Are there particular challenges the team or company is facing right now that this role will help address?
Who will be my primary collaborators? Will there be cross-department cooperation?
How would you describe the company culture or the work environment?
Is there anything I could highlight in my application that would be especially valuable for this position?
How does the onboarding and training process usually work for new employees or consultants?
What does success look like for this role in the short and medium term?
For me it is important to know the main challenges in the role, the culture, and what success means for the team. Could you tell me about those?
What would I need to do to meet and exceed expectations at my first performance review?
You mention {N} years of {experience type}. How important is the number of years compared with experience actually {doing the core work, e.g. leading projects from concept through delivery}?
questions.use_when: The candidate misses a stated years-of-experience requirement but has the substance.

questions.text: How is the time split between {main task in the ad} and {secondary task in the ad}?
questions.use_when: The ad lists two kinds of work, e.g. new development and after-sales upgrades.

questions.text: The ad mentions {method or certificate}. How formally do you use it, and is certification expected?
questions.use_when: The ad names a method or certificate the candidate knows but is not certified in.

questions.text: I have done {core work} as {actual title}, not with the title {title in the ad}. What would you most like to see in my application to judge that?
questions.use_when: The candidate has the experience under a different job title.

questions.text: Who makes the final call when {two goals in the ad, e.g. cost and specification} pull in different directions?
Can you give an example of a project or idea the team stopped, and how that decision was made?
